howto: Rediger .new-felt, så kjør node tools/story-tool.js build. Bildefelter (name/look/verbs/intro/endings) skrives tilbake. Dialoger (readonly) redigeres i JS-filene.

texts.old: In an age before ages got late,
the Great Rings were forged in the factories of Middle-earth.
Three for the elves. Seven for the dwarves. Nine for men –
and one to rule them all … plus the service agreement.
But one day, the Great Ring went missing.
It turned up in the pocket of UNCLE BONGO,
a retired adventurer who refused to believe it was more than loose change.
"Probably from a vending machine," he said. He said it often. Nervously.
Now the Dark Lord's Vice-Chancellor has booked a pickup.
The only one who can save the neighborhood is a small halfling
with big feet and a poor sense of planning:
TOMBLE BAGSHOT. That is you. Sorry.
THE END — the good kind!
The Ring screamed "NOOO! I had SO much left to give!"
and melted away with a tiny confetti-bang.
The Dark Lord lost his job and opened a bakery instead.
Uncle Bongo flew past on an eagle: "I TOLD you I would come!"
Rando's first comment: "So the food at your uncle's WAS free, right?"
THE END … or is it?
Tomble kept the Ring. The Ring kept Tomble.
Three weeks later he was middle manager at Mordor Inc.,
in charge of meeting minutes and evil looks.
The pay was poor. The coffee was worse.
Uncle Bongo sent a card: "Regards, grandma. PS: My ring?"
Bloomdale. Nine in the morning. The birds are singing, the grass is green, and someone has packed an entire house into boxes.
Uncle Bongo? Why is all your furniture standing out in the garden?
Stick
Apple
The Great Ring
Pouch of coins
Tin whistle
Salted sausage
Mug of ale
Lucky spoon
Boathouse key
Oar
"Mordor Times"
Uncle Bongo
Uncle Bongo. He has reading glasses on his forehead and the Ring in his eyes – in that order.
You cannot pack uncles. They arrive voluntarily.
Ew. We are RELATED.
Uncle Bongo… why is all your furniture in the garden?
The Ring, Tomble. THE Great Ring. I inherited it from my uncle, who inherited it from HIS uncle.
We are clearly terrible at throwing things away.
My glasses? They must be in a box… or a pocket… or…
Uncle Bongo characteristically reaches for his forehead. There sit the glasses. They have ALWAYS sat there.
Found them. As always. Not a word of this to anyone.
You seem worried. What is going on?
Are you even fit to travel? You keep hunting for your glasses.
Why are you moving out again?
Billy the Goat
A goat. She is evaluating me as a food item that has feelings.
BAAAAH.
Black Rider
Toll. One coin. Or a favor. Or just some company. This shift is LOOOONG.
Mordor Roadworks. We operate a toll station now. Payment accepted in coins, information or entertainment.
Nobody has paid since Tuesday. LAST Tuesday.
I AM a dark power. You know what it\'s like working in the family business? Like that. But with more cloak regulations.
A toll? Out here?
What kind of favor are we talking?
Aren\
Give him the Mordor Times.
Something to READ. I have been staring into this road for six weeks. Even the gravel avoids eye contact now.
Dora (innkeeper)
Dora, innkeeper of The Wobbly Pony. She is drying a mug that was already dry. Twice.
The innkeeper is not on the menu. People have asked.
The bar is served FROM behind it. Not ON it. Compose yourself.
Welcome to The Wobbly Pony! We serve soup, beds and scandal. What will it be?
Halvor Halfpint
Halvor. His elbow rests on the table. The table does not rest back.
He is heavy. And he has friends. Well, ONE friend. The table.
Heyyy! Table is my best friend. I like YOU too. About the same amount.
I am NOT drunk. I am… horizontally optimistic. *hic*
You look like someone who needs something. Everyone needs something. I need something to DRINK.
Your spoon… it was pretty… gonna just… close my eyes a bit… *hic*
Rando the Wanderer
A dark wanderer in the corner, trying very hard to look mysterious. It works slightly too well.
He weighs roughly as much as a library with shoulders.
Psst. Over here. No – HERE. I\'m just your average mountain wanderer™. No special background. No secrets.
You are sitting in the shadows, staring dramatically at the door.
Exactly. Standard wanderer behavior.
Rando. Rando the Wanderer. I guarded the south road for three years. Before that: two years guarding another road.
I have seen things. Things you wouldn\'t believe. Among them: a man eating soup with a fork.
Dangerous? Nah. Just a Black Rider running a toll booth, a troll with poetic ambitions, and a volcano with a renovation plan.
…Maybe a LITTLE dangerous.
Who ARE you exactly?
Is the road to Mount Pleasant dangerous?
Will you come with me?
On an adventure? Without a contract? Hmm. What are the stakes? What is the pay? What about–
Grim Greybeard
Grim Greybeard, fisher-gnome. He stares at his bobber like it owes him money.
He is small but tough as tar. And he has friends. Many, many fish friends.
Do not disturb a man mid-conflict with a catfish.
TODAY? Yesterday I landed a catfish so big she had her own postal code.
Proof? Proof is for people who get believed.
Hungry? I am SO hungry I considered eating the bait. The bait is A HOOK.
What I need is real food. Salty. Meaty. Sausage-shaped, if you must know.
If he follows you: hit him with something long. Or give him a fish. No – hit him.
Small catch today?
Aren\
Who is that grey thing sneaking by the rock?
Trade a salted sausage for an oar?
Hm. Tourist. Fine. Fish don\'t bite on tourists anyway. Already tested.
Something grey behind the rock
Two big, wet eyes peek over the rock. They seem to recognize you. That worries me most of all.
*hissing* Don\'t touch! Glum is gentle! Glum is FRIENDLY! Almost!
*hissing* You have it, yes? WE know you have it. It SCREAMS. The whole river screams.
Have what? I have many things. I have a sausage. Do you want the sausage?
NOT THE SAUSAGE! *hissing* THE TREASURE. My treasure! I mean… nobody\'s treasure. Officially. *dives*
Bent the Bridge-Troll
My bridge. My rules. My poems. Also my go-backwards.
HALT! My bridge, my rules. Payment accepted in POETRY.
Poetry? Not coins? Not blood?
Pass, poet friend. And greet the lava for me. We have… history together.
You already paid. In VERSE. G onward.
Goblin
*growl* Goblin has knife. Goblin has mood. Don\'t ruin the mood.
*sniff* Hobbit! Soft! Good with mustard! …No wait. We are on a DIET. Leader\'s orders.
(They aren\'t listening to me. But they ARE listening FOR me. Which is almost worse.)
Zzzz… five gold rings… two small… one BIG one… zzzz…
Bjarne (guard)
Bjarne the orc. He wears a hi-vis vest OVER his chainmail. Safety first, tradition later.
Do not touch the vest. It is certified by the workplace safety board of TWO ages.
CLOSED. Maintenance. No entry. No, you can\'t just– no. Read the sign. The sign is CLEAR.
Glum
Glum. He oscillates between "menace" and "pleading". The distance between them is shorter than you think.
*hissing* Glum helps! Glum only wants treasure to bathe! A little! Only a bit!
Throw it! Don\'t throw it! THROW IT! Don\'t– GLUM! Calm yourself!
Glum is TWO goblins in one body. It is difficult for EVERYONE.
the round door
A round green door built into the hillside. Uncle Bongo claims green doors are "classic". He said the same about his trousers.
Locked. Uncle Bongo loses keys constantly. Or the keys lose him.
the round window
Someone has drawn a moustache on the inside of the glass. Suspect: Uncle Bongo. Evidence: everything.
the neighbor's window
The neighbor's round window. Warm light inside. Their moustache drawings are less impressive.
the tin whistle
A tin whistle resting on the door step. It lies there as if waiting for a musical moment. Or an excuse.
the woodpile
Neatly stacked firewood. Uncle Bongo calls it "pension plan B".
The wood was stacked by a man with strong opinions about angles.
a loose stick
A sturdy stick leaning by the woodpile. It has lain here long enough to form opinions about the neighborhood.
the apple tree
A small apple tree full of red apples. They hang high. Arrogantly high.
The tree wobbles a little. The apples laugh at you.
They hang too high. Even for a hobbit on tiptoe.
an apple
One perfect apple. It fell from a great height with style.
the moving boxes
Boxes marked "FRAGILE". Uncle Bongo has corrected it to "FRA-GIL-E" in pencil. Twice.
No. Opening other people's boxes is how adventures go BAD.
the fence post
A sturdy fence post. Someone has carved "BLOOMDALE RULES" into it. Both letters and grammar are questionable.
The post stands firm. Respect.
the east gate
The gate toward the eastern road. The world outside Bloomdale waits. It smells slightly less like cocoa.
the signpost
Two arrows. One points west ("Bloomdale"), one points east ("Grumblingdale"). Below, less legible: "and otherwise just around".
The signpost creaks, alarmed.
the crows
Two crows. They are judging me. The left one has already written the verdict.
the mailbox
A red mailbox with its flag raised. The flag means complaint. The postal service knows this road well.
a crumpled newspaper
"MORDOR TIMES – all the news, one opinion." The headline is set in CAPITALS and zero discussion.
the hollow log
A hollow log. Classic hiding spot. Even I have read adventure stories.
You peer inside. Something peers back. It is your reflection. PROBABLY.
The log weighs roughly as much as my future regrets. It stays.
the dead tree
Even the trees have given up out here. Respect for the honesty.
The tree groaned. It was not enthusiastic.
the north path
A narrow path wanders north between the hills, toward the sound of running water.
the road home
The road back toward Bloomdale. The cocoa at home calls faintly.
the east road
the fireplace
The fire crackles away like Uncle Bongo's knees. The warmth is real. The coziness is debatable. The warmth is real.
You warm your hands. Adventure requires warm fingers and cold feet. Or something.
the bar counter
The bar top has been polished by a thousand elbows. Human elbows. The other kind charge by the hour.
the bottle shelf
Bottles from every corner of Middle-earth. Some of them still remember the Roman Empire.
Dora coughed. From across the room. Impressive lung work.
the picture on the wall
A small landscape painting. It hangs slightly crooked. Like everything else in this establishment.
You straighten it. It tilts back within the minute. Some things are meant to be.
the window
Outside it is evening. Inside there is soup. The balance of the universe holds.
Halvor's table
Two empty mugs. Halvor refers to them as "colleagues".
The mugs are empty. Like Halvor's promises.
a plate of salted sausage
A salted sausage on a plate. The pride of the house. Dora winks: "Take two." I take one.
something shiny
A silver spoon under the table! Halvor apparently "inherited" it down to the floorboards.
the arched doorway
The exit. The door to the crossroads and the rest of the story.
the road west
The path back toward the crossroads and the tavern. Civilization faintly whispers about soup.
the reeds
Reeds. They stand perfectly still. Either they are wise, or they are terrible at dancing.
The reeds sway. Somewhere a fish gives a tiny round of applause.
the dock
Wooden planks in varying states of "safe". Some of them are only theoretically attached.
You test a plank. It passes the test. Barely.
the river
The river glitters. Somewhere out there a fish is having a better day than you, and it knows.
You dip a finger in. Cold. The river does not judge you. The river has no time for that.
the fish bucket
Grim's bucket. It contains one fish. The fish stares. You CAN lose a staring contest to a fish.
The fish blinked first. You lost.
the BOATHOUSE sign
"BOATHOUSE" – hand-painted with one extra letter's worth of confidence. Friendly folk along this river. Creative, at least.
The sign hangs crooked. Like so many other things in life.
the boathouse door
the rowboat
the path west
The path back toward the riverbank. The reeds wave goodbye. They are good at standing still and bad at farewells.
the owl
An owl. She has seen everything. She judges gently. That is somehow worse than harsh judgment.
the goblin campfire
A fire built by goblins. Rare hospitality – right up until you wonder what they usually set ON fire.
You poke the fire. Sparks dance. No goblin protests. Yet.
the goblin camp
glowing mushrooms
Mushrooms that glow. Either they are magical, or there is a party going on in the roots. Either answer is fine.
Edible? Unclear. Glowing? Yes. The math argues against dinner.
the hollow tree
You knock on the tree. Inside it echoes hollowly. Or almost hollowly. Depending on the evening.
the decorative lantern
A lantern without oil, without flame, without purpose. Pure decoration. Exactly like back home.
*click click*. Nothing. The lantern is more ornament than light source. Like Uncle Bongo's diploma on the wall.
the bridge
An old stone bridge across a ravine. The bridge is solid. The figure on it looks less solid. He looks like a bridge WITH OPINIONS.
the road over the bridge
the path back
The path back toward Trollwood and the bridge. Bent is probably still composing.
Mount Pleasant
Mount Pleasant. The name was chosen by a tourism board. The volcano was NOT consulted. It smokes, offended.
You cannot climb an entire volcano on attitude alone.
the warning sign
"FIRE HAZARD" with a skull. Thanks. Very helpful. I would NEVER have guessed that a volcano was hot.
The sign wobbles, threatened. Even the signs are tired out here.
the dragon sign
"NO PARKING FOR DRAGONS." Something has parked here anyway. The tracks are large and hurtful to the grass.
No dragons in sight. The rules hold. For now.
the lava crack
A crack with glowing contents. It smells like Uncle Bongo's kitchen when he "experiments".
No. We dip NOTHING into lava until we have thought VERY carefully. ESPECIALLY not fingers.
the queue barrier
A queue barrier. The queue is empty. People rarely line up for an active volcano. Mystery solved.
You step into the queue. You are number one! And number everything. Congratulations.
the guard desk
The guard desk. Form FD-66: "Application to Throw Things Into Lava", in triplicate, stamped by someone who no longer exists.
The papers are stacked according to a system only Bjarne (and possibly the lava) understands.
the iron gate
the CLOSED sign
"CLOSED FOR MAINTENANCE – reopens next age." Below, in smaller print: "(sorry for the inconvenience)"
The sign swings a little. It has no power left here. Not over you, at least.
the lava
Below: lava. Lots of lava. a CONCERNING amount of lava. It bubbles like soup at Dora's, just more ambitious.
No. We do not throw things in RANDOMLY. We throw things in WITH A PLAN. Or not at all.
the broken sign
"DO NOT THROW THINGS HERE!" – the sign itself lies half inside the crater. The house of irony has found its headquarters.
The sign gave up on its own rule. Respect for following through.
the crater rim
